subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today, Emily — really appreciate the clear context on Atlas Payments' evaluation goals. Per our discussion, I put together a short recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the POC success criteria. Please flag anything you'd like changed.

Recap (high level):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for real-time payment routing and fraud classification at Atlas scale, with predictable latency and cost.
- Scope: inference for charge authorization flow (avg. payload size ~250 tokens).
- Duration: 3-week trial (pilot environment), followed by production sizing conversation.

Proposed POC success criteria / KPIs:
1) Latency: P95 end-to-end inference latency < 200 ms for single-request flows (target), with P99 < 350 ms under pilot workload.
2) Throughput: sustain 150 reqs/s steady-state per instance group, with autoscale headroom to 500 reqs/s for burst windows.
3) Cost: inference cost <= $0.0008 per token (target) at quantization Q4 model and batching enabled; measure cost/token across requests.
4) Quality: top-intent accuracy >= 92% on your labeled eval set; false positive rate for fraud flags < 0.5% (we'll use your labeled test-set).
5) Reliability: successful responses > 99.5% (no server errors), and graceful fallback to smaller model with minimal degradation in quality.

Measurement plan:
- We'll run an A/B eval where ~10% of traffic (shadowed or replayed) hits Redwood pilot env against your golden set.
- We'll provide dashboards for token counts, latency P50/P95/P99, cost breakdown, and model-quality metrics tied to your eval prompts.

Timeline & ownership:
- Target start: 2026-06-01
- Pilot duration: 3 weeks (2026-06-01 -> 2026-06-21)
- Jordan (me): POC lead / primary contact
- Marissa: Customer success / onboarding and quality evaluation
- Marcus: Engineering lead on performance / integration
- Alex: Infra / deployment & devops contact

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the start date and provide the evaluation dataset + a sample production traffic window you want us to emulate?
- We'll send a short POC SOW and the test plan (attached) once you confirm.

Attachments: 20260520-redwood-poc-proposal.pdf (POC SOW), poc-test-plan.xlsx (detailed test scripts & metric collection)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Thanks Jordan — this is great and very close to what we discussed. A few quick questions before we confirm dates: 

1) For latency targets, are the numbers client-side (our service -> Redwood -> client) or server-side (model inference only)? We need to make sure we're comparing apples to apples with our current infra numbers.
2) For the cost / token target, can you confirm whether that assumes 8-bit quantization and continuous batching? Also, how do you want us to share representative tokenization stats (avg tokens per request)?
3) We can provide the labeled eval set next week. For the traffic window, typical peak is ~120 reqs/s for the auth flow during the US morning spike; we want to validate up to 400 reqs/s as a safety margin.

If all that aligns, let's aim to start 2026-06-01. We prefer the pilot to run in your hosted sandbox unless you recommend a VPC for this first test.

Emily
EMILY CHEN
Head of ML Engineering
Atlas Payments

To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Great questions — answers below so we have a clear record.

1) Latency: the targets I listed are end-to-end server-side (Redwood inference time + network hop to our API edge). To map to your client-side metrics we'll add an instrumented measurement that includes your service-to-Redwood network latency so you can compare directly. We'll provide both server-side and client-observed numbers in the dashboard.

2) Cost assumptions: the $0.0008/token estimate assumes using an 8-bit quantized model (Q4) with continuous batching and a 256-token average for billing. If your avg tokens/request is lower, cost/token will be lower. Please share a sample of token counts; we can run quick estimates.

3) Load: 120 reqs/s typical peak, validating to 400 reqs/s — noted. We'll size pilot instances accordingly and include a higher-load soak test on week 2.

Hosted sandbox vs VPC: for speed of start we recommend hosted sandbox for week 1 (fast onboarding), with the option to flip to a private VPC slice if you prefer for weeks 2-3. Either way we can provide the same metric collection and audit logs.

Attached is the poc-test-plan.xlsx with the scripted workload and KPI collection points. We'll follow the plan below:
- Week 0 (pre-provisioning): share dataset + access; integration checklist
- Week 1 (baseline): run traffic ~120 reqs/s, collect latency/cost/quality
- Week 2 (stress & regressions): ramp to 400 reqs/s, run soak, check fallbacks
- Week 3 (validation & handoff): quality eval and runbook for production sizing

I'll get Marissa to schedule the kickoff and I'll loop Alex for infra details.

Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Couple of technical clarifications and how we'll measure each KPI from Redwood side: 

- Latency measurement: we'll report P50/P95/P99 at two points — model-serve (inference-only) and end-to-end (edge + inference). We'll also export histograms so Atlas can recompute percentiles.
- Throughput: we'll run both constant-rate load (120 reqs/s) and burst tests to 400 reqs/s. We'll report sustained throughput per node and cluster-level capacity.
- Cost/token: we'll instrument tokenization at the ingress and record token counts per request; cost will be calculated using actual GPU cycles + batching efficiency — reported as $/token and $/1000 requests.
- Quality: Marissa will drive labeling, but we'll also run a shadow evaluation where we score Redwood outputs against your golden set and compute top-intent accuracy, precision/recall for fraud tags, and a small human review sample.

A note on fallback behavior: we'll configure automatic fallback to a smaller model family when queue latency exceeds 500 ms; we'll record quality delta for those requests. If Atlas wants deterministic rollbacks we can set up a canary policy instead.

I'll prep a short runbook for how we collect artifacts for your SOC/PII review if needed.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
